verdict.rationale: ComplyAdvantage documents a Batch Processing API and asynchronous screening for high-volume scenarios, so a first-party bulk-processing path exists. Nothing in the evidence shows import job status tracking, per-record error reporting, or resuming after partial failure, and the batch mention appears only in the customer-screening context. Missing for 10: documented batch job status/progress tracking, per-record failure reporting, resume/retry of partially failed batches, bulk transaction import coverage, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can track bulk customer and transaction imports and resume after partial failure

citations.quote: For high-volume processing, use the Batch Processing API.
Asynchronous screening: Suitable for high-volume screening scenarios
